## 2026

**Monday 5th October 2026 — Tony Short** (University of Bristol)

<details class="abstract"><summary>Click to expand abstract</summary>
Recurrence of finite quantum systems

*As a finite quantum system evolves, different initial states will evolve very differently. However, it is possible to find a time at which all states return arbitrarily close to their initial configuration. We obtain bounds on the time for this recurrence, by linking it to the mathematical problem of approximating real numbers by rationals.*

*(based on arXiv:2604.14995)*
</details>

**Monday 19th October 2026 — Habib Rostami** (University of Bath)

<details class="abstract"><summary>Click to expand abstract</summary>
From Hidden Collective Modes to Nonlinear Response in Quantum Materials

*Collective excitations and nonlinear responses provide powerful probes of symmetry, interactions, and quantum geometry in condensed matter systems. In this talk, I will discuss three theoretical developments: demon and Fano-demon modes in altermagnets, nonlinear quantum Hall transport in interacting Dirac systems, and a quantum-geometric theory of light-induced Raman forces. Together, these examples highlight how symmetry, electronic interactions, and quantum geometry shape collective phenomena and nonlinear light–matter responses in quantum materials.*
</details>

**Monday 2nd November 2026 — Chaim Goodman-Strauss** (Museum of Mathematics, New York)

<details class="abstract"><summary>Click to expand abstract</summary>

The Monotiling problem and other questions

(Joint Maths Colloquium / Theoretical Physics seminar)

*The famous Penrose tiles, the hat monotile Dave Smith discovered in 2023, and the very new, LLM-found, three-dimensional Chair44 are aperiodic: they shapes that can form tessellations, but only non-periodic ones. The discovery of aperiodic monotiles suggests the "Monotiling problem" (whether or not a given shape can form a tessellation) may be computationally undecidable. We'll survey a web of similar questions about monotiles.*

</details>
